items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: But we worked on a couple of projects... So we would work together on things like that.

ctx.x: What attracts DownBeat to people who write reviews on books and records?

Yeah. I think it’s, I think there are writers who like their art along the road less traveled. It’s like we are more interested in high art than pop art. And I think that they tend to be very thoughtful, very well read, very educated, very very — you know before they were jazz writers they were jazz record collectors. I don’t know of anybody who wasn’t a jazz record collector beforehand and they fell in love with the liner notes of, you know, Nat Hentoff and all the greats, you know, so those are the things that…

I remember that too and I’d go to the record store and you’re flipping through and sometimes it was the cover, but then you flip that thing over and sometimes you even learned about the reviewers and you learned well I like this reviewer, if he likes this record I’ll buy it.
